title: Lecture 14 — Vector equations of lines and planes
summary: Describe a line using one direction and a plane using two independent directions or a normal, and move between vector and coordinate equations.
body: A parameterized line starts at a chosen point and moves along one fixed direction. Every coordinate must use the same parameter; restricting its range selects a segment. A plane adds a second independent direction, or equivalently imposes a dot-product constraint with a nonzero normal. These descriptions let you check membership, construct a plane through three noncollinear points, and convert between vector and scalar equations. The examples emphasize checking all coordinates and recovering a normal through orthogonality. In higher dimensions, distinguish a two-parameter plane from the hyperplane defined by one scalar equation. Exercise 14 follows Algebra section 1.3.
